Herculano-Houzel et al. 2020 Methods 2.1: "For all specimens except Chaerophon pumilus, we had only one hemisphere available for quantitative analysis ... data are necessarily expressed as twice the numbers obtained for the available hemisphere, to make them comparable to other mammalian species in our dataset; for C. pumilus, numbers provided refer to the sum of both hemispheres." Table 1 marks each species (1H each) or (2H each). PUBLISHED AS 2x one hemisphere: used as published, never doubled again. The (2H each) species is in laterality_known_exceptions.csv. The brain mass of the same table (MBRAIN) is registered in the next row.

Brain mass of Table 1. The paper does not say in words whether it is a brain weighed whole or the sum of the dissected structures; its own numbers decide it (HerculanoHouzel_etal_2020/internal_checks/HerculanoHouzel_etal_2020_TABLE3_internal_check.csv). MBRAIN equals the sum of the structure masses implied by Table 2 (neurons / neurons per mg) within rounding for 5 species and within 1.41% for all 13, and the species measured on both hemispheres (Chaerephon pumilus) differs from that sum as much (-1.38%) as the one-hemisphere species do (differences of that size are what means over two animals give). MBRAIN is therefore the sum of the dissected structures, on the same basis as the neuron numbers: PUBLISHED AS 2x one hemisphere for the (1H each) species. Used as published, never doubled again. Registered 2026-11-24; no value changed.
